events.text: You wake in the pavilion above the cloud-sea and someone you love is sitting at the end of the bed, saying good morning. You know the face, the voice, the laugh, the way they hold the cup. You open your mouth for their name and there is nothing there. Not forgotten the way a word is forgotten: lifted out. On the sill lies a single strand of silver hair that is not yours.

choices.text: Pick up the strand

effects.log: It hums faintly, a note you almost know. Somewhere an exile is singing.

choices.text: Say good morning back and hide it

effects.log: You say good morning. You do not say the name. Nobody notices yet.

events.text: Last night you read the final scroll of a forbidden cloud-scripture, deeper than anyone is supposed to read it. This morning your own household stands around your bed, worried, calling you by your name, and you can only look from face to face and say: you, and you, and you. The scripture is lying open on the desk. The last line is gone from the page.

choices.text: Burn the scripture

effects.log: It will not burn. The silk goes red and cold. That is the first clue.

choices.text: Draw each face, so you do not lose those too

effects.log: You draw them badly and write under each: someone I love.

events.text: The breakthrough in the Purple Palace went wrong in the night. The qi ran backwards through the memory sea and scoured it like a tide going out. In the morning your body is whole, your cultivation is whole, your arts are whole. It is only that the people you love have become someone, someone, and someone.

choices.text: Go back into seclusion to find the damage

effects.log: You find a hall of rooms, every door still there, every nameplate washed blank.

choices.text: Go out and spend the day with them anyway

effects.log: They do not need you to say their names to be glad you are here. It helps less than it should.

events.text: The one you married has begun leaving little notes about the pavilion, in a careful hand: on the tea-tray, on the door, on the pillow. Each says the same short thing. You read them aloud to yourself, in the dark, and a word is missing from every one. 'It is all right,' someone says gently from the doorway. 'I know where you are.'

choices.text: Hold the notes against your heart

effects.log: They crackle. You hold them all night.

choices.text: Say sorry, and mean it

effects.log: A quiet 'I know' from the doorway.

events.text: Your children come home for the festival, and one of them asks, offhand, if you have decided what to call the new lantern-boat. Their tone is kind and tight. All of them have noticed that you say 'sweet one' and 'little one' and never any name. The smallest takes your hand without a word.

choices.text: Name the boat anything at all

effects.log: You name it Morning, which is no one's name. The children laugh.

choices.text: Tell them what has happened

effects.log: They listen. The eldest nods and says: 'We will lend you ours.'

events.text: A friend on the Isles writes you a long letter and you reach the end without once being able to say whose hand wrote it. The signature is a drawn crane, which you recognise. The warmth you feel for the writer is real. The name for it is gone. You read the letter to the empty room until you have it by heart.

choices.text: Write back with no name at all

effects.log: You write: dear friend. The reply is a single line: that is enough.

choices.text: Keep the letter, unanswered

effects.log: It sits in the lacquer box and gathers dust.

events.text: At the Jade Court's autumn audience a clerk calls for one of your kin to come forward to be recognised, and you cannot rise to say who. The Keeper looks at you for a moment and says kindly, 'Take your time.' The hall waits. Your hands on your knees are cold. Someone behind you coughs.

choices.text: Say plainly that you have lost the name

effects.log: The Keeper writes it down without comment. You are not the first.

choices.text: Name someone else and move on

effects.log: A mistake that hurts a stranger.

events.text: An old cloud-singer on the shore of the Sea of Clouds, blind, says she remembers an immortal who drank names: Seo Hwa the Mist-Singer, exiled from the Isles for singing a stranger's name off its owner. 'She sings at the edge of the cloud-sea at dusk,' says the old singer. 'Take a clean cup if you go.'

choices.text: Thank her and take a clean cup

effects.log: She presses a second cup into your hand, unasked.

choices.text: Ask what the cup is for

effects.log: 'To hold the song,' she says. 'And to give it back.'

events.text: You find Seo Hwa's old pavilion, shuttered, its door tied with a faded ribbon. Inside, rows of empty cups on a long shelf, each with a thread of mist coiled in the bottom like a sleeping thing. Each cup has a tiny tag. The tags are blank. You hear, very faintly, a woman's voice singing from somewhere under the floor.

choices.text: Follow the song

effects.log: A trapdoor, a stair, a lower room.

choices.text: Take one cup and go

effects.log: The cup is warm. The mist in it turns toward you.

events.text: Seo Hwa sits at the end of the lower room with a cup in each hand, thin as a reed, pale as the mist. She looks at you and sings one clear note, and one of your names comes back and goes again like a fish in water. 'To break it,' she says, 'you must make me want to give them back. Do you know anything that would?'

choices.text: Offer her a name of your own, willingly

effects.log: She takes it as one takes a coin. 'It is a start.'

choices.text: Offer her a story of the Isles she has missed

effects.log: Her eyes fill. 'Tell me everything,' she says.

events.text: The librarian of the Hall of Quiet Scrolls tells you there were nine copies of the cloud-scripture once, and that each reader forgot something. 'The first forgot his breath,' says the librarian. 'The third forgot her songs. The last forgot who he loved. We burned the eight. The ninth went missing.' You have a feeling you know where.

choices.text: Ask where the ninth went

effects.log: 'Into a reader,' says the librarian. 'Always into a reader.'

choices.text: Ask how it was reversed

effects.log: 'It was not,' says the librarian. 'But I have read of a cure.'

events.text: The cure is in a book that is not in the Hall: a dream-primer, written by a dreamer who read the scripture and lost four names. She marked how she got them back, one by one, by finding where the names had gone. 'Names do not vanish,' she wrote. 'They fall into the places they were last spoken.'

choices.text: Make a list of those places

effects.log: Fourteen places, over a hundred years of life. You begin.

choices.text: Start with the place closest to your heart

effects.log: A courtyard. A bench. A tree.

events.text: At the stone bench under the plum tree you say, aloud, what you remember: the shape of the laugh, the weight of a head on your shoulder, the sound of a name you cannot say. The plum tree drops one white blossom into your hand. It is warm. It has a taste you recognise, and a smell, and almost, almost, a word.

choices.text: Eat the blossom

effects.log: It tastes of her smile, or his. You are not sure which.

choices.text: Press it into a book

effects.log: The book is the dream-primer. The page it falls on is blank.

events.text: A physician-immortal of the Star Sea Pavilion who studies deviations tells you, kindly, that qi turned backward in the Purple Palace usually scours the sea of memory. 'It leaves the knowledge and takes the attachments,' she says. 'Names are attachments. The good news: they leave a scar, and scars can be followed.'

choices.text: Ask how to follow it

effects.log: 'By sitting still in the place the qi turned,' she says. 'And feeling for the warm spot.'

choices.text: Ask what to do if there is no warm spot

effects.log: She does not answer at once.

events.text: In the empty Purple Palace at dusk you sit where the qi turned and feel for the scar. There is a cool place, and beside it a warm one, the size of a cup. You put your palm on it. A name tries to rise, and sinks again. A smell of wet stone. A sound of someone laughing in a hall far away.

choices.text: Stay longer, and breathe slowly

effects.log: The warmth grows. It has the shape of a name, nearly.

choices.text: Mark the place for next time

effects.log: You tie a ribbon round the nearest pillar.

events.text: The physician teaches you the Circle of the Seven Breaths, a slow method for refilling the memory sea with its own tide. Seven breaths for each name, in order, and a pause between that is the length of a held heart. The first three come easily. At the fourth, you feel something shift, deep and faint.

choices.text: Finish the seven

effects.log: It takes the whole evening. At the end your cheeks are wet and you have not said a word.

choices.text: Rest and try again tomorrow

effects.log: Rest helps. Sleep is full of faces.

events.text: A year goes by on a road that turns out to lead nowhere. The informant was lying, or wrong, or dead. You come back to the pavilion with dust on your hem and no more than you started with. The cranes in the garden look at you, a bit sadly. Someone puts a cup of tea in your hands without being asked.

choices.text: Drink the tea and begin again

effects.log: You do.

choices.text: Sit a while with the someone who brought it

effects.log: They sit with you. It is enough for a night.

events.text: You spend a season in the Hall of Quiet Scrolls following a rumour of a cure that turns out to be a poem. It is a beautiful poem, about a woman who forgot the sea. At the end the librarian looks at you with sympathy. 'There are no easy ones,' says the librarian.

choices.text: Copy the poem anyway

effects.log: It is a comfort of sorts.

choices.text: Burn your notes and breathe

effects.log: Smoke goes up. You feel lighter.

events.text: You wait at the shore of the cloud-sea for a month for an immortal who does not come. The tide goes in and out. The sea is quiet. When you finally leave, you do it without bitterness. Not every road is a story.

choices.text: Leave a lantern on the shore

effects.log: In case the immortal comes late.

choices.text: Walk back the long way

effects.log: It takes three days. You see the Isles properly.

events.text: Seo Hwa lifts her cups one by one and pours them into the sea, and a pale light runs up the water to your feet and into your chest, and the names come back like a held breath let go. All of them. In order. You say each one under your breath. When you look up, the exile is gone and the cup on the rock is empty.

choices.text: Say every name aloud, to the empty shore

effects.log: The sea carries them to wherever she is.

choices.text: Leave a cup of tea for the singer

effects.log: By morning it is empty.

events.text: The last name returns at the plum tree on a day of rain. You are sitting on the bench with the dream-primer in your lap and the blossoms coming down, and something small and bright slides back into the place it belongs. It is like a coin falling into a bowl. You say the name aloud. It is the best sound you have ever made.

choices.text: Go and find them at once

effects.log: You run.

choices.text: Sit a while and let it settle

effects.log: The name is yours. It stays.

events.text: The seventh breath of the seventh circle holds, and a long unfolding opens in the sea of memory: rooms, doors, nameplates freshly lettered in a hand you have always known to be your own. The names come back one at a time like lamps being lit down a long corridor. You walk the corridor to the end.

choices.text: Walk out into the garden

effects.log: The people you love are there, and you know every name.

choices.text: Write them down in the hall's registry

effects.log: In ink, in order, in your own hand.

events.text: The ritual fails. The mist does not come, or it comes and goes, or the scripture says the wrong word. You sit for a long time in the room afterward with your hands open on your knees. A name rises, very close, and does not break the surface. Tomorrow you will begin again. Tonight you only breathe.

choices.text: Breathe and hold on

effects.log: The night passes.

choices.text: Say the loved faces aloud, one by one

effects.log: It does not bring the names, but it does bring the faces.

events.text: Your attempt to follow the scar ends in a dizzy blur and a taste of copper. A healer of the Star Sea Pavilion puts you to bed with a bowl of broth and a stern look. 'You pushed too hard,' says the healer. 'Names do not come by force.' You lie in the dark, tired, and listen to the cranes.

choices.text: Rest, as told

effects.log: You rest.

choices.text: Plan the next attempt

effects.log: A gentler one.

events.text: A method that worked for another sufferer does not work for you. You are told that cures are like keys: a fine key, made for another lock. The librarian offers tea and says there are other doors. You do not hear it kindly yet. The cranes do.

choices.text: Let the librarian be kind

effects.log: Tea, and silence, and a pat on the shoulder.

choices.text: Say you will try the next door

effects.log: The librarian gives you the list.

events.text: It happens at the market, in the dull middle of the afternoon, with a crowd going by and a cloud-boat unloading: you turn and see a face, and the name comes, small and clear, and you say it before you can stop. '{nc_name},' you say. The one you said it to stops, and looks at you, and does not move. 'Say it again.'

choices.text: Say it again, and again

effects.log: {nc_name}. {nc_name}. The market watches, kindly.

choices.text: Take their hands and say nothing more

effects.log: Their hands are warm. You do not need to say it twice.

events.text: You do not expect it in the middle of a cloud-barge voyage, in the middle of a conversation about nothing, but there it is: {nc_name}, as natural as breath. You say it. The one beside you grips the rail. 'You said my name,' they say. 'You said it like you used to.'

choices.text: Say it as you used to

effects.log: It comes out easy. It always did.

choices.text: Let them hear it again

effects.log: The sea listens.

events.text: You wake before dawn with a name on your tongue. It is the first time in years. You say it, softly, to the ceiling, and the ceiling is a kind listener. Then you get up, and walk across the Isles in the dark, and knock on a door. '{nc_name},' you say, when it opens. The face behind the door crumples, and then smiles.

choices.text: Hold {nc_name} close

effects.log: Neither speaks. The cranes begin their morning song.

choices.text: Stay for breakfast

effects.log: There is plenty to say.

events.text: Some names will not come back, and you know which. They are the names of those who are gone: you cannot ask them, and nothing in the Isles can tell you. You carry their shapes instead of their names. It is a way of remembering, and you have grown used to it. At a shrine, you leave a cup of tea for someone.

choices.text: Leave the cup

effects.log: Someone drinks. You are sure of it.

choices.text: Light a lamp without a name

effects.log: The lamp does not need one.

events.text: A very old immortal tells you, in the Garden of Remembering, that the dead keep their names for themselves, and that this is not a loss but a courtesy. 'They have put them away to give you room,' he says. It is the kindest nonsense you have ever heard, and you find you need it.

choices.text: Thank him

effects.log: He bows and goes back to the plums.

choices.text: Say it is not nonsense

effects.log: He is delighted.

events.text: You have lived with the curse a long while, and a kind of peace has settled on it. You love by the shape of a laugh, a hand on the shoulder, a way of pouring tea. The names are gone, but the loves are not. The Isles are used to you now: the one who says 'friend' and means it entirely.

choices.text: Say 'friend' with all of your heart

effects.log: It lands. They know.

choices.text: Make a game of guessing the old names

effects.log: They guess, you laugh, nobody is right. It is a joy.

events.text: A new young household moves into the next pavilion and asks politely what to call you. You say: 'Neighbour.' They say: 'Neighbour, then.' By spring it is the most loved name on the Isle, and the funny thing is that it fits you better than the old one ever did.

choices.text: Accept the new name

effects.log: It stays, warm and light.

choices.text: Teach them the old names you still know

effects.log: You tell them stories. The children listen.

events.text: A cloud-scribe in the Hall of Quiet Scrolls looks up when you enter and says, 'Oh. You again,' though you have never been. Then, embarrassed: 'Forgive me. You have the face of someone who once asked me to write down names that would not stay written.' The scribe looks away, and you have a sudden desire to cry.

choices.text: Ask who it was

effects.log: 'I never knew,' says the scribe. 'I remember only the ink was cold.'

choices.text: Thank the scribe and say nothing

effects.log: The old feeling comes again, light and sorrowful.

events.text: In the plum garden of a house you are visiting, you stop at a bench you have never seen, and put your palm on the wood. It is warm. You feel a name there, almost. 'We have a legend about that bench,' says your host. 'It remembers people. Go on, sit.' You sit. The tree drops one white blossom into your lap.

choices.text: Keep the blossom

effects.log: It never withers.

choices.text: Ask your host the legend

effects.log: Something about a reader and a lost name. Your skin prickles.

events.text: A street-singer on the edge of the Sea of Clouds sings a cup-song, soft and wavering, about a woman who drank a name by mistake. You stop. You do not know the song, and yet every word is in you. The singer finishes and holds out her bowl. You put in a stone, and the singer says: 'You knew it. Why?'

choices.text: Say you do not know

effects.log: The singer nods as if you had said something true.

choices.text: Sing the last verse yourself

effects.log: It comes out clear. The singer weeps.

events.text: {sac_name} sets down the lifespan-lamp on the table between you and turns the wick low so it will not show how little oil is left. For six hundred years {sac_he} has stood at the same rung. 'The tribulation clouds will not come for me,' {sac_he} says. 'I have asked. I would rather you heard it from me than from the lamp.'

choices.text: Take {sac_his} hand over the lamp

effects.log: The flame leans toward your fingers, as if it knew.

choices.text: Say: 'Then we will find the door.'

effects.log: {sac_name} does not argue. {sac_He} looks as though someone has handed {sac_him} a spare year.

events.text: At the old cloud-pavilion where you swore the oath of sworn kin, {sac_name} pours two cups of mist-wine and does not drink. 'I am stuck, brother-in-arms, sister-in-arms, whatever we are. Six hundred years at {sac_realm}. My years are going. I am telling you because the oath says we do not lie to each other.'

choices.text: Raise a cup to the oath again

effects.log: You raise it. The tea tastes of a younger Isle.

choices.text: Make {sac_him} tell you every attempt

effects.log: {sac_name} tells you all of them. You find yourself counting what you could give.

events.text: {sac_name} was born into your house when the White Stairs were new. Now {sac_he} meets you on the old porch, looking thinner than a cultivator should. 'I am out of years at this rung. Do not tell the house. They will turn the family hall into a funeral before I am gone.'

choices.text: Promise to keep it

effects.log: You keep the promise. You also start doing sums with your own years.

choices.text: Say the house deserves to know

effects.log: {sac_name} looks stung, then relieved. 'Perhaps they do.'

events.text: {sac_name}, who you have walked beside on the Isles for longer than most mortals' dynasties last, finally says it over a pot of cloud-tea: the rung will not open, the years are running out, and {sac_he} has accepted it. {sac_He} asks about the weather in the Sea of Clouds, as though nothing has been said.

choices.text: Answer, and keep the secret

effects.log: You talk about the weather. Inside, you are counting what you have that could be given.

choices.text: Refuse to change the subject

effects.log: 'No. We are talking about this.' {sac_name} looks relieved that someone has said it.

events.text: {sac_name} comes out of a long seclusion in a robe that hangs loose and silver-grey at the temples. Hair that was black for six centuries went pale in a month. 'Close,' {sac_he} says. 'It was close again.' The cranes in the garden look at {sac_him} and fold their wings.

choices.text: Bring a Mid-grade stone for the next attempt

effects.log: The stone helps the body. It does not help the rung.

choices.text: Sit with {sac_him} through the night

effects.log: {sac_name} sleeps for the first time in weeks.

events.text: A disciple half {sac_name}'s age passes the rung at the Jade Void Sect's autumn trials and bows to {sac_him} with great respect. {sac_name} bows back perfectly, and afterwards breaks a jade cup in {sac_his} hand without noticing. The pieces glitter on the floor like frost.

choices.text: Take the pieces out of {sac_his} palm

effects.log: {sac_name} lets you, and does not speak for a while.

choices.text: Say the disciple was lucky

effects.log: {sac_name} laughs, bitterly, and agrees. It helps a little.

events.text: {sac_name} asks you to look at the calendar of the Isles with {sac_him}: a long scroll of festivals, moon-feasts, anniversaries. 'I want to mark which ones I will see,' {sac_he} says. Most of the scroll is blank. You mark them together, one by one, until the ink runs dry.

choices.text: Mark every one, even the far ones

effects.log: {sac_name} smiles. 'You are an optimist.' You are not.

choices.text: Mark only the near ones, truthfully

effects.log: The scroll shrinks. {sac_name} takes your hand.

events.text: You spend the Festival of Floating Lanterns beside {sac_name}, on a barge that does nothing but drift. {sac_He} watches the lanterns going up through the mist and does not once mention the rung. You learn what a person looks like when they are trying very hard to enjoy something for the last time.

choices.text: Let the lanterns say it for you

effects.log: You release one with {sac_name}'s name on it. It rises too slowly.

choices.text: Ask what {sac_he} wants from the rest of the years

effects.log: 'Nothing hard,' says {sac_name}. 'Tea. Company. The cranes.'

events.text: {sac_name} teaches you the last form of an art that will die with {sac_him}: a slow sword-dance of the cloud-sea, taught only by touch. You learn it badly. {sac_He} corrects your wrist as if it were the most important thing in the Isles, which today it is.

choices.text: Practise until dark

effects.log: You are better by evening, and bruised.

choices.text: Ask {sac_him} to teach it to someone younger too

effects.log: 'Yes,' says {sac_name}, after a long moment. 'That is a good idea.'

events.text: {sac_name} wants to see the Stars of Autumn from the cliff above the sea. You carry two cushions and a flask up the long path. At the top {sac_he} lies back and says the stars look different when you have only a few hundred years to look at them. They look exactly the same. You both say they do not.

choices.text: Lie back beside {sac_him}

effects.log: The stars hold still for a long time.

choices.text: Say the stars have waited this long

effects.log: 'So can I,' says {sac_name}. It is not a promise.

events.text: It is done. The channel of your cultivation ran from you into {sac_name} through your joined hands, one bright thread, and you felt yourself becoming lighter and plainer. {sac_name} opens {sac_his} eyes and sees the sky differently. 'I can feel it,' {sac_he} whispers. 'The door. It is open.'

choices.text: Sit with {sac_him} while it settles

effects.log: The first night of {sac_realm} is the best night either of you remembers.

choices.text: Say nothing of what it cost

effects.log: You smile. It is the smile you are best at.

events.text: You gave a realm of your own to {sac_name}, and the thing about a gift of that size is that you feel the shape of the empty place for the rest of the day. {sac_name} crosses the rung in the hall of the House of Falling Stars. The cranes lift off the roof. Some of them are crying out.

choices.text: Watch the cranes go

effects.log: You stand in the quiet, lighter and stranger.

choices.text: Help {sac_name} through the first hour

effects.log: {sac_He} is unsteady. You hold {sac_his} elbow until it passes.

events.text: You gave two realms, and you did not tell {sac_name} it was two. You told {sac_him} it was one. {sac_He} will find out the sum in the years ahead, when {sac_he} counts what is missing from you. For now {sac_He} is only luminous, and you are tired in a way that sleep cannot reach.

choices.text: Rest, and let the secret keep

effects.log: You sleep for three days. {sac_name} watches the door.

choices.text: Tell {sac_him} the truth that night

effects.log: {sac_name} is silent for a long time. Then {sac_He} bows to you with both hands.

events.text: The hall of the House of Falling Stars is quiet after the second realm crosses. {sac_name} looks younger than {sac_he} has in centuries. You look like someone who has had a long illness and recovered. 'You gave me too much,' {sac_he} says. 'Take it back.' It is not possible. You both know that.

choices.text: Say it was freely given

effects.log: The phrase hangs in the hall. {sac_name} bows.

choices.text: Say you will earn it back

effects.log: You do not know that you will. You say it anyway.

events.text: The rung opened by itself. No gift, no ritual, no sacrifice: just a morning after a hundred sleepless nights, when {sac_name} walked out into the garden and the sky leaned down to meet {sac_him}. You were not there. You hear it from a sweeper, secondhand, and then {sac_He} is at your door, laughing.

choices.text: Embrace {sac_him}

effects.log: You hold on, and {sac_he} laughs, and the cranes circle. The gift you had been planning stays in your hands.

choices.text: Ask what it was like

effects.log: 'Like putting down a bucket,' says {sac_name}. 'I did not know how heavy it was.'

events.text: {sac_name} wrote to say it was over, and not in the way you feared: the wall gave. The letter is two lines long. Beneath it, a pressed cloud-lily, which in the Isles means: I am no longer waiting. You read it at the window and then you read it again.

choices.text: Write back with a feast date

effects.log: The feast is the loudest in your pavilion's memory.

choices.text: Keep the letter in the book you love most

effects.log: It sits between the pages.

events.text: You were about to offer. You had it prepared, the words, the ritual, the number of realms. Then a messenger tells you that {sac_name} passed the rung in the night, quietly, without help, and is taking visitors in the morning. You sit down with the speech still in your mouth.

choices.text: Go in the morning with flowers

effects.log: You say none of the speech. You hold the flowers.

choices.text: Keep the speech for another day

effects.log: You may need it for someone else.

events.text: {sac_name} went into the last seclusion alone and did not come out. You learn it from the hush of the pavilion on the third morning, and from the cranes standing on one leg and not looking at anything. The Jade Court's Keeper writes the line in the Rolls. The lamp on the table has gone out.

choices.text: Light the lamp one more time

effects.log: It burns with a small steady flame. You leave it burning.

choices.text: Walk the garden {sac_he} loved

effects.log: The cranes follow you at a distance.

events.text: The seclusion door stays shut. After seven days the disciples knock, and after seven more, the elders open it. {sac_name} is sitting upright in meditation with a look of calm on {sac_his} face, as though a long argument had ended in agreement. You did not give anything in time. That is the thing you will carry.

choices.text: Sit in the empty seclusion room

effects.log: It smells of cold tea and old paper. You stay until dusk.

choices.text: Go to the Rolls and read the line

effects.log: It is short. You read it many times.

events.text: There is a feast on the day of {sac_name}'s memorial, as is the custom in the Isles: fruit, wine, and a seat left empty. You sit near the seat, and keep to tea. A young crane, which has never seen {sac_name}, lands on the empty cushion and refuses to leave.

choices.text: Let the crane stay

effects.log: It stays through the whole feast and the long night after.

choices.text: Pour a cup for the empty seat

effects.log: The wine soaks into the cushion. Somehow it is right.

events.text: {sac_name} calls on you with a gift: a small jade tablet inscribed with every season since the day of the crossing. 'I counted,' {sac_he} says. 'Each one is a year you gave me. I am not thanking you. I am showing you what you did.' The tablet is heavier than jade has any right to be.

choices.text: Hang the tablet by your door

effects.log: Visitors ask what it is. You say: a friend's accounts.

choices.text: Ask {sac_him} to read the seasons aloud

effects.log: {sac_name} reads them all. It takes an afternoon.

events.text: At {sac_realm}, {sac_name} is among the elders of the Jade Void Sect, and at the autumn gathering stands to speak on the nature of sacrifice. {sac_He} does not look at you. {sac_He} does not need to. The hall knows. Afterwards a dozen young cultivators ask you what it was like to give a realm away.

choices.text: Say it was the easiest thing you did

effects.log: They go quiet.

choices.text: Say you would do it again

effects.log: And you would.

choices.text: Say you do not talk about it

effects.log: They respect that.

events.text: {sac_name} brings you a bowl of the first plums of the year, which only grow on the south slope of the Nine Clouds Palace. 'I know,' says {sac_name}, before you can speak. 'You like them. You never say so. I have been listening for six hundred years.' Eating them is a small ceremony that neither of you names.

choices.text: Eat slowly and say nothing

effects.log: The plums are sweet. The silence is better.

choices.text: Tell {sac_him} what the gift meant to you

effects.log: {sac_name} listens as though to a hymn.

events.text: Decades on, {sac_name} stands on the White Stairs at dawn, bowing to nobody in particular. 'I meant to do it every day,' {sac_he} says when you find {sac_him}. 'It is not the stairs. It is that there are mornings. Because of you there are mornings.' The mist is rose-coloured. You stand beside {sac_him} and bow too.

choices.text: Bow beside {sac_him}

effects.log: Two bows on a long stair.

choices.text: Say you did only what a friend would

effects.log: {sac_name} shakes {sac_his} head and says no.

events.text: A cultivator you have just met offers you a cup of tea at a road shrine and looks at you with a warmth that does not belong to strangers. You feel it too: a cup, a table, a lamp turned low. {sac_past} is the name that rises in your mind, and you cannot place it. The tea tastes of home.

choices.text: Ask if you have met before

effects.log: 'Not in this life,' says the stranger, smiling.

choices.text: Let the warmth be warmth

effects.log: You drink. It is enough.

events.text: You find yourself standing before a gate at the edge of the Isles, with a lamp in your hand and no memory of lighting it. Someone you have never met is waiting on the other side. Their face is one you would give your life for, and you may have. {sac_past}: it is the only name you have.

choices.text: Open the gate

effects.log: The stranger bows. It is a bow you know.

choices.text: Hold the lamp and say the name

effects.log: The lamp flares.

events.text: The Keeper of the Lotus Ledger turns a page for you, unasked, to a line of ink from an older life: a vow, a gift, a name you recognise in your bones. {sac_past}. The Keeper says nothing about it. You say nothing back. But you ask, quietly, to be shown the rest of the page.

choices.text: Read the page

effects.log: The ink has not faded, and neither has the debt, or the love.

choices.text: Close the Ledger gently

effects.log: Some pages stay shut for a reason.

events.text: The Isle War is over and the hall of {wo7_foe} on the south reef is a ruin of snapped beams and torn silk. In the crane-loft above the broken stair you find a child sitting among the empty perches, holding a single grey feather. {wo7_name} does not cry. {wo7_He} looks at the sigil on your sleeve and decides, visibly, to be brave.

choices.text: Sit down on the perch-boards beside {wo7_him}

effects.log: You sit. After a while {wo7_name} leans on your arm. The cranes will not be back.

choices.text: Wrap {wo7_him} in your cloak and name {wo7_him} yours

effects.log: The child is very light. You will have to be someone's parent by morning.

choices.text: Carry {wo7_him} to the barge as a hostage

effects.log: The rank on your sleeve opens every door. Behind you, {wo7_name} keeps hold of the feather.

choices.text: Raise a white banner and take {wo7_him} home

effects.log: You tie a white sash to your sleeve and walk toward the enemy lines with a child's hand in yours.

events.text: Searching the wreck of a grotto of {wo7_foe} for ledgers, you find none. You find a child asleep inside an empty spirit-stone chest with the lid propped open on a hairpin. Someone made a bed in there, and left air. A tag on the collar reads {wo7_name}, and under it: whoever finds this, please.

choices.text: Close the chest softly and think

effects.log: You close the lid on the hairpin and sit with your back to it. Nobody else is allowed in this room.

choices.text: Lift {wo7_him} out and call {wo7_him} your own

effects.log: {wo7_name} wakes, sees your face, and decides to believe the word own.

choices.text: Report the find, with the child

effects.log: The barge captain writes it in the day's log. The word hostage appears at the end.

choices.text: Search for the child's kin before dark

effects.log: You leave a trail of folded paper cranes toward the white-banner camp.

events.text: Three days after the war, the Ministries' clerks are still counting what was won. You walk the hanging gardens of the fallen house of {wo7_foe} and hear a small voice reciting a counting rhyme to no one. It comes from a bell-tower where a child sits with both knees up, saying the numbers over and over to keep fear out.

choices.text: Climb up and say the next number

effects.log: You say it. {wo7_name} stops, stares, and finishes the rhyme with you.

choices.text: Say you will be the child's guardian

effects.log: The word guardian travels quickly through the Isles. You will answer for it later.

choices.text: Sign the child over to your side's ledger

effects.log: You write the name in the Rolls column for captives. Your hand does not shake. It should.

choices.text: Ask who is waiting for {wo7_him}

effects.log: A name comes out. It is an elder of the enemy, alive, three isles away.

events.text: The old crane-keeper {wo7_keeper} lives on a far isle where the wind never turns and nobody asks where a child comes from. {wo7_keeper} looks at {wo7_name}, looks at your sleeve, and says only that the loft there has plenty of room and the cranes like children.

choices.text: Leave spirit stones for the winters

effects.log: The stones go into a tea tin. The tin goes on the highest shelf, and is counted twice.

choices.text: Promise to visit each spring

effects.log: A promise to a child is the longest kind on an island. You make it anyway.

choices.text: Teach {wo7_name} to ride a crane in case of flight

effects.log: One lesson, one fall, one grin. You have hidden the child and also, a little, armed {wo7_him}.

events.text: The cloud-barge takes you out of the war zone under a false lading of salt-fish. {wo7_name} spends the voyage inside a barrel, narrating the sea in whispers. Somewhere over the Sea of Clouds {wo7_He} asks if the sky is where the war goes when it is finished.

choices.text: Say yes, and mean it

effects.log: The lie is kind. You will owe the sky for it.

choices.text: Say you do not know where wars go

effects.log: {wo7_name} nods as though this is the honest answer, and the only one worth having.

events.text: At a customs tower the Ministries' inspectors tap every barrel with their staves. When the staff comes near the one with the child in it, you start a loud argument about the price of salt. By the time it is over, three inspectors are bored and one has forgotten which barrel he was looking at.

choices.text: Pay the inspectors off with a Low-grade stone

effects.log: The stone is the best bribe you will ever make.

choices.text: Keep arguing until they let it go

effects.log: You are hoarse, and the barge is through.

events.text: The Rolls of the Jade Court have a column for every new household member. You stand at the registry stair with the child's hand in yours and the clerk's brush above the page. The clerk waits. {wo7_name} waits. The ink drips.

choices.text: Write the name in as one of yours

effects.log: The brush moves. {wo7_name} is now in the Rolls, in your house, under your sigil.

choices.text: Say the child is a ward, not a child

effects.log: The clerk makes a note. The word ward buys you time, not safety.

choices.text: Walk out and raise {wo7_him} unregistered

effects.log: There is no record to find, and none to protect {wo7_him} either.

events.text: Your first night as a parent of the enemy's child. {wo7_name} will not sleep in a bed, and sits on the floor of the guest pavilion, watching the door. You put your blanket down beside {wo7_him}, lie with your back to the room, and say good night to the dark.

choices.text: Stay on the floor all night

effects.log: You wake with a stiff neck and a small hand fisted in your sleeve.

choices.text: Leave a lamp lit

effects.log: The lamp stays lit all winter.

events.text: At the House of the Silent Bell's spring feast an elder looks at {wo7_name}'s face and then at yours and asks, pleasantly, whose sleeve the child was cut from. The table goes still. {wo7_name} stares into a cup of plum wine and does not touch it.

choices.text: Answer with a proud, flat lie

effects.log: The elder smiles the way people smile at a good lie. You are watched for a year.

choices.text: Say: 'Mine. Now pass the wine.'

effects.log: A silence, then a nod. Something has been settled at that table.

events.text: The hostage hall of your own side is a gracious room with good tea and a locked door. {wo7_name} sits in the corner and does not cry. You are told the child is an asset. You are told to keep out of the way of the clerks who will decide what asset means.

choices.text: Visit every day, and bring sweets

effects.log: By the tenth day {wo7_name} says your name. You hate how that feels.

choices.text: Keep away, as ordered

effects.log: Rules are rules. The hall's tea goes cold in your memory.

choices.text: Ask the clerks what the child is worth

effects.log: A number. You feel sick all the way home.

events.text: Your side wants {wo7_foe} to know that the child is safe and in its hands. A letter is drawn up, and you are asked to sign as a witness. The letter is polite. The letter is also, plainly, a leash.

choices.text: Sign, and add a line in the margin

effects.log: Your margin line says the child is in good health and well fed. It is the only kindness the letter holds.

choices.text: Refuse to sign

effects.log: The clerks note your refusal. Nobody argues. Everybody remembers.

events.text: A stern officer of the Celestial Ministries tells you that all enemy children are being sorted by spirit-root. Strong roots will be taught at the Ministries. Weak roots will be sent to far isles. {wo7_name}'s root, on testing, is the colour of a clear dawn.

choices.text: Ask to be named the teacher

effects.log: The officer smiles for the first time. Teaching is better than sorting.

choices.text: Ask for the child to be sent to a far isle

effects.log: Better a far isle than a Ministries cell. You write to a keeper you know there.

events.text: The white banner is a very small thing on a long pole, and you carry it across three isles of no-man's-sky with a child on your shoulders. Nobody fires. Wars have habits, and one of them is that a white banner on a plain pole is, for one afternoon, a road.

choices.text: Walk tall and say nothing

effects.log: The hush around you is the most solemn you have felt in a century.

choices.text: Sing the counting rhyme with {wo7_name}

effects.log: The rhyme carries over the water. Even the pickets lower their bows.

events.text: At the edge of the enemy lines a veteran of {wo7_foe} steps out, hand on a sword, and stops. {wo7_name} climbs down from your shoulders and walks forward very slowly. The veteran kneels on the cloud-stone. They do not speak. A long breath goes round the whole camp.

choices.text: Bow to the veteran and step back

effects.log: The veteran bows back. A thread of understanding runs across the war.

choices.text: Stay a moment to be sure the child is safe

effects.log: You stay. The veteran hands you a cup of barley tea without being asked.

events.text: The white banner worked, and then did not: on the way home your own side's barge-guards stop you and ask why a Ministries officer was seen on the wrong side of the line. You say you were returning lost property. The guard-captain takes a long time to put that sentence in the log.

choices.text: Show the proof of the child's safe return

effects.log: A letter from the veteran, unsigned, with a feather pressed in it. It buys your name back.

choices.text: Say it plainly, and take the reprimand

effects.log: The reprimand comes with a Low-grade fine and a nod from someone behind the captain.

events.text: Someone has counted heads in the loft and found one too many. A summons arrives on the tide: the Ministries want you at the Cloud Terrace to explain a child of {wo7_foe} sleeping under your sigil. The summons is polite. Summons from the Terrace always are.

choices.text: Defy them: the child stays

effects.log: You walk into the Terrace with your hands empty and your answer ready. The child stays where it is.

choices.text: Yield the child to the Ministries

effects.log: You hand over the name, and the child with it. You will remember how light {wo7_name} was.

events.text: The elder of your own pavilion, Old Master Serin, finds the secret out from a sweeper and puts it to you in the empty practice hall at dusk. 'I can burn the report, or I can send it up. I would like one reason to do the first.' The elder looks old tonight.

choices.text: Give the reason: the child has done nothing

effects.log: Serin listens, and pours two cups of cold tea. The report will burn.

choices.text: Say you will send the child away yourself

effects.log: Serin nods. 'Good.' But the nod is sad.

events.text: It was a servant, a kindly one who thought the Ministries would reward a good citizen, and who now stands at your gate wringing hands. The Ministries have sent two clerks and a guard. The clerks have the child's name on a list, and the list has a column for your answer.

choices.text: Defy the list and shut the gate

effects.log: The gate shuts. It will not stay shut.

choices.text: Open the gate and read the list

effects.log: The list is long. The child is one of two hundred names. Yours is at the bottom.

events.text: An old man arrives at the foot of the White Stairs in a robe the colour of the fallen house, with nothing in his hands. He gives no name. He asks, with perfect courtesy, whether any child of {wo7_foe} has been seen in these Isles, and watches your face while he waits.

choices.text: Give the child back to the old man

effects.log: He takes the child's hands in both of his and cannot speak for some time.

choices.text: Say you have seen no such child

effects.log: He looks at you for a long time and goes away. He will be back.

events.text: A woman of the enemy house arrives on a cloud-barge with a young boy beside her, to ask if you have news of her niece. She says the girl is in the Rolls as lost. She asks nothing else. She sits on your steps with her bundle and waits as if the steps were a river and she a heron.

choices.text: Bring {wo7_name} out to meet them

effects.log: A cry, an embrace, and the whole yard goes quiet. The aunt looks up at you over the child's shoulder.

choices.text: Send them away with food and silence

effects.log: They go, and the barge turns north. You listen to it for a long time.

events.text: A letter comes under no seal, in the old script of the fallen house: they are looking, they will not stop looking, and they are not angry. The name signed is one you recognise from the lists of the dead. You turn it in the light. It is only a message on a dead woman's paper, written by someone alive.

choices.text: Write back: the child is safe

effects.log: The reply comes by crane at midnight. {wo7_name} reads it over your shoulder and laughs for the first time.

choices.text: Burn it and say nothing

effects.log: The ashes are grey. You still smell them in the morning.

events.text: {wo7_name} has stopped asking whether the war is coming back. {wo7_He} asks instead for the names of constellations, the shape of the bridge in the market, why the old women on the isle feed the gulls. These are the questions of a child who intends to stay.

choices.text: Answer every question

effects.log: You are tired by the evening and happier than you expected.

choices.text: Say you will find the answers together

effects.log: {wo7_name} considers this and agrees, with dignity.

choices.text: Let {wo7_him} wander and learn alone

effects.log: Some questions are better left to find their own answers.

events.text: {wo7_name}'s first cultivation lesson goes wrong in the funniest way: a ring of spirit-mist rises from the child's breath and swallows the whole tea-table. You pull a small stern face out of the cloud, and a very small grin. 'Is that normal?' {wo7_name} asks, delighted.

choices.text: Say it is perfectly normal

effects.log: It is not. You will write to someone about it.

choices.text: Laugh until you cannot stand

effects.log: The child laughs with you. The laughter is the best medicine on the isle.

choices.text: Ask {wo7_him} to do it again

effects.log: Twice is a pattern. You begin to see an art in it, and wonder whose.

events.text: At the end of the rainy season {wo7_name} stops sleeping with the feather in a fist and puts it on the windowsill instead, between a snail shell and a button. {wo7_He} does not mention it. You do not mention it. But the room feels different with the feather on the sill.

choices.text: Keep the sill clean and say nothing

effects.log: You wipe the sill every morning. The feather stays.

choices.text: Put a second feather beside it

effects.log: {wo7_name} stares at the pair. 'Where did you get that?' 'A crane gave it to me,' you say.

events.text: A year after the war, {wo7_name} builds a small shrine in the corner of the garden: three stones and a blue ribbon. {wo7_He} does not say whose it is. Each morning {wo7_He} sets a cup of water on it, and each evening takes it away.

choices.text: Add a stone, quietly

effects.log: One stone, set in the dark. The child notices at dawn and says nothing, which is a great deal.

choices.text: Ask whose shrine it is

effects.log: 'Mine,' says {wo7_name}. 'For the ones I do not have names for.' You sit there until the water is cold.

choices.text: Leave the shrine to the child

effects.log: It is {wo7_his} to keep. You keep your distance, and your hands off.

events.text: {wo7_name} comes home from the market with a black eye and a refusal to say whose. The older children had said things about where the child comes from. {wo7_He} said something back in the old script, and the market learned some very pointed words that day.

choices.text: Clean the eye and ask nothing

effects.log: A cool compress. By morning the quarrel is half forgotten.

choices.text: Teach {wo7_him} a guard that costs nothing

effects.log: A bow, an open palm, a step back. {wo7_name} practises until the sun goes down.

events.text: {wo7_name} has been quiet for a month, and tonight comes to the door of your pavilion and asks without preamble: whose child am I? Whose house? The question has been under the floor of the house for years. The lamp is low. The answer, if you give it, will be the longest speech of your life.

choices.text: Tell the whole truth, now

effects.log: You say it all: the war, the loft, the ruin of {wo7_foe}. {wo7_name} hears it in silence.

choices.text: Tell the truth, but gently, in pieces

effects.log: A piece tonight, a piece in spring. It is slower, and kinder, and not quite the truth.

choices.text: Say the past does not matter

effects.log: It is the one answer {wo7_name} does not believe.

events.text: At the Lantern Festival a woman in a veil presses a paper crane into {wo7_name}'s hand and whispers a name. The child comes to you with the crane unopened and a face the colour of the sky before rain. 'Is this me?' {wo7_He} asks. The crane is trembling, though nobody is touching it.

choices.text: Open the crane together

effects.log: Inside is a house crest, a mother's name, a street. It is all true.

choices.text: Tell {wo7_him} to ask again in a year

effects.log: A year is a long time for a child to hold a crane. {wo7_name} nods, and does.

events.text: You take {wo7_name} up to the roof of the old pavilion at midnight, where the cloud-sea laps the ridge-tiles, and say: I need to tell you where you come from. The child does not speak. {wo7_He} listens as the stars go out one by one. At the end, {wo7_He} asks only if the cranes were kind.

choices.text: Tell {wo7_him} the cranes were kind

effects.log: It was true. You are not sure how you know.

choices.text: Tell {wo7_him} you do not know

effects.log: It is also true. {wo7_name} takes it with a nod.

events.text: {wo7_name} has learned the truth from a veteran's boast at a tavern, and comes to you in the evening with it, shaking. It would be easy to hate. {wo7_He} sits down opposite you and says: 'You could have left me. They all said you should.' The silence after is as quiet as a closed book.

choices.text: Say you almost did

effects.log: The truth is the only gift you have. {wo7_name} takes it, and takes your hand.

choices.text: Say you would not have been able to

effects.log: It is also true. {wo7_He} is crying, and it is the good sort.

choices.text: Say nothing and pour tea

effects.log: Some thanks need a cup of tea more than words.

events.text: You told {wo7_name} yourself, and the child took it hard, and then gently. Now, on the anniversary of the war, {wo7_He} asks you to light a lamp with {wo7_him} for the house of {wo7_foe}. 'Not for the war,' {wo7_He} says. 'For the ones who cannot be thanked.' You light it together.

choices.text: Say the names you know, aloud

effects.log: You know some of them. The lamp burns longer than it should.

choices.text: Light it in silence

effects.log: The silence has weight. The child leans on your shoulder.

events.text: A chest in the attic opens under {wo7_name}'s hands: a ledger, the pavilion's own, with your side's sigil on the cover and entries about the last day of the fallen house. {wo7_He} reads it by candle for an hour. When {wo7_He} looks up, there is nothing of the child left in {wo7_his} face.

choices.text: Say you did not write it

effects.log: It is true, and no help. The silence in the room becomes a wall.

choices.text: Offer to answer every question

effects.log: {wo7_name} asks one: 'Were you there?' You were.

choices.text: Let {wo7_him} leave in the night

effects.log: The door stays open. The tea goes cold.

events.text: You told the truth first, and still {wo7_name} could not forgive it. {wo7_He} packs light, with the grey feather in a pocket. 'I thank you for telling me,' {wo7_He} says at the door, 'before someone else did. That is why I am walking and not running.' The door closes on a child you did not lose, and did.

choices.text: Say you will be here when the walking ends

effects.log: You say it to the closed door, which does not answer.

choices.text: Let {wo7_him} go with a purse of stones

effects.log: The purse is gone from the table by morning, and so is the feather.

events.text: A sealed silk roll was sewn into the hem of the child's old coat. {wo7_name}, grown now, unpicks it carefully and lays it on your table: the lost cloud-weaving art of the fallen house, a pattern of eighty-one threads thought burned in the war. {wo7_He} offers it to you the way one offers a house key.

choices.text: Study it together

effects.log: Six months of evenings, four hands on one loom. By spring the pattern is half alive.

choices.text: Ask {wo7_him} to keep it for the house

effects.log: 'The house is gone,' says {wo7_name}. 'I am what is left. I would like it to be yours too.'

events.text: {wo7_name} stands up at the small ceremony you hold on the anniversary and recites, from memory, an entire star-chart of the fallen house: a night-sky manual forgotten by every other scholar in the Isles. When the recital ends there is quiet, and then the oldest elder of your pavilion begins, slowly, to applaud.

choices.text: Offer the chart to the Jade Court's Rolls

effects.log: The Keeper accepts the chart. The Isles will see stars the war forgot.

choices.text: Keep it between the two of you

effects.log: It is a small private treasure, and a heavy one.

events.text: A box arrives from {wo7_name}: not a message, a box, wrapped in silk the colour of the fallen house. Inside is a spirit-lamp whose flame shows the shape of every stone it is held to. A note in the old script says: this is how my people found their way home. I have found mine.

choices.text: Light it in the window

effects.log: The light finds the shape of the house you are standing in, and the child you raised.

choices.text: Study the lamp's making

effects.log: The lamp is a method. You learn more about the old house in one evening than in a hundred years of war.

events.text: A figure stands on the White Stairs at dusk in the grey of the fallen house, and you know the walk before the face. {wo7_name} is grown, and is here to be heard. The anger has not gone. It has sharpened, and been put away, until now. 'I want the truth,' {wo7_He} says, 'and I want to see how well you can stand.'

choices.text: Stand your ground, as an equal

ok.log: You stand, and the stairs hold. Eventually {wo7_name} lowers a raised hand.

fail.log: You are the older cultivator, and still the stairs shake. {wo7_name} walks off with the matter unsettled.

choices.text: Sit on the step and talk

effects.log: The step is cold. You say everything you ever meant to. It takes until dawn.

choices.text: Lower your hands and take whatever comes

effects.log: {wo7_name} does not strike you. The tears come first.

events.text: {wo7_name} comes back to the isle at the head of a company of the enemy's remnant and asks for you by name, not by rank. The company halts at the gate. {wo7_He} walks in alone. 'I loved you,' {wo7_He} says, in a voice you have to lean toward. 'I want to know if it was real.'

choices.text: Show the old loft feather you kept

ok.log: The feather turns in your palm. {wo7_name} stops, and smiles for the first time in years.

fail.log: The feather means nothing to a grown person with a war to settle.

choices.text: Say it was real, and say how

effects.log: You tell the story of every winter. It takes the whole night.

choices.text: Kneel on the stones of the yard

effects.log: The yard is silent. The company outside the gate lowers its banner.

events.text: A message by crane: {wo7_name} wants to meet at the ruin of the loft, alone, at the turn of the tide. You go. The loft is a shell now, perches rotted and sky showing through. {wo7_He} stands in the doorway with the setting sun behind. 'Everything I am is in this room,' {wo7_He} says. 'Tell me what you did here.'

choices.text: Draw your power and stand it down

ok.log: The air hums and settles. {wo7_name} nods once, like a judge, and sits.

fail.log: You falter. {wo7_name} sees it, and leaves with more questions than answers.

choices.text: Describe what you did, step by step

effects.log: You say each thing. The child listens as a judge does.

choices.text: Bow your head and say nothing

effects.log: A long stillness. A tear on the old boards.

events.text: {wo7_name} and you share a pot of tea on the roof at dawn, the first since the reckoning. Neither speaks of it. The cloud-sea is gold, and a grey crane circles twice and lands on the rail. 'They always come back,' says {wo7_name}. For the first time in years, it is not a question.

choices.text: Sit and watch the crane

effects.log: The crane stays an hour. It is the longest hour of peace you have had.

choices.text: Offer {wo7_him} the second cup

effects.log: It is taken. The first sip is silent and the second is a laugh.

events.text: The house of the fallen is a ruin, but a door has been cut in the wall, and above it hangs a new lamp: yours, given and received. {wo7_name} lives in one house and visits the other, which the Isles think odd and the two of you do not.

choices.text: Hang a second lamp beside it

effects.log: The pair of lamps burns through the night. Passers-by remark on it.

choices.text: Walk through the new door

effects.log: It opens inward, with a sound like a breath let go.

events.text: {wo7_name} has gone, and the pavilion is quieter than the ruin of the war ever was. You find the grey feather on the sill, set out squarely. A note beneath, in the old script: not goodbye, not yet. You are not sure what it means, and you are very sure you will wait for it.

choices.text: Keep the feather on the sill

effects.log: It stays there for centuries.

choices.text: Write a letter you cannot send

effects.log: The letter fills ten pages. It is burned for warmth that winter.

events.text: Years later a trader from a far isle mentions a young cultivator who teaches cloud-weaving to orphans, with a grey feather in a ribbon at the throat. You do not ask the name. You pay for the trader's tea twice, and send three pots of the good leaves along, unlabelled.

choices.text: Send a plain letter with the leaves

effects.log: A single line: whenever you wish.

choices.text: Let the tea speak for you

effects.log: A pot of good tea is a very old kind of letter.

events.text: On the day {wo7_name} takes a place in the Jade Court's Rolls, the Keeper reads the sponsor's line aloud: your name. The hall hears it. The child bows to you in front of the whole court, low and without pride, and the court, which was prepared for a scandal, finds itself applauding.

choices.text: Bow back, just as low

effects.log: The two bows cross like swords of a different kind.

choices.text: Say it was the child's own merit

effects.log: It is only partly true, and you say it anyway.

events.text: Ages have turned in the Isles' reckoning when {wo7_name}, already a master, brings a student to meet you. 'This is my teacher's teacher,' says {wo7_He}. The student bows to someone named in four generations of silk-weavers' prayers. You never learned to take a compliment, and you do not learn today.

choices.text: Teach the student the first stitch

effects.log: One stitch, and a hundred years pass through it.

choices.text: Wave them all off and make tea

effects.log: Tea is the right answer.

events.text: The child you handed over has grown in the Ministries' halls and risen. Today there is a letter in the Ministries' seal: {wo7_name} has been named a magistrate of the south reef. The letter is courteous, and does not mention you at all. That is its own message.

choices.text: Send your congratulations anyway

effects.log: A card with two lines. No reply. A year later, a small gift.

choices.text: Keep the letter and say nothing

effects.log: You keep it in the desk with the others.

events.text: You see {wo7_name} once more, across a hall of the Ministries, in the grey robe of a clerk. {wo7_He} is thin and straight. {wo7_He} looks at you, and then through you, as one looks through a window to a view that has been bricked up. The door opens and the clerk is gone.

choices.text: Let it be

effects.log: Some doors do not reopen. You carry this one too.

choices.text: Send word that the door is open

effects.log: You send it, a single line. It sits unanswered for a long time.

events.text: A white banner is raised over the old pavilion, and {wo7_name}'s kin have returned to restore it. They send you a bolt of silk the colour of the dawn and a lamp-oil flask sealed with the old crest. The silk is fine. The silence under the gift is a thank-you in another script.

choices.text: Wear the silk to a Court feast

effects.log: It is a quiet statement. Several people understand it.

choices.text: Keep the silk folded in a trunk

effects.log: Some gifts are best admired in the dark.

events.text: A year after the white banner, a young woman of the old house comes to the isle with a basket of figs and a note from the child, now grown: 'I am well. Someone told me about you in the year I was ten. I did not understand then.' The basket is very heavy with figs, and with something else.

choices.text: Send the basket back, full of tea

effects.log: The balance is kept.

choices.text: Eat a fig, slowly

effects.log: They are very sweet. You think of the loft.

events.text: {wo7_name} lives on the far isle with the old crane-keeper, and has never been named in any Roll. Nobody who counts knows the child exists. Years pass in the rhythm of wing-beats. A message arrives at the turn of each season: well, fed, happy. You read each one twice and burn it.

choices.text: Keep the secret until your last day

effects.log: Some secrets are the best thing you ever did.

choices.text: Visit the isle once more

effects.log: You ride out in the early light. The cranes remember.

events.text: A cloud-barge from the Ministries stops at the far isle for water and nothing else. The crane-keeper serves the crew tea and talks about the weather. The child is in the loft with a feather in a fist and does not make a sound. When the barge leaves, the cranes begin to sing.

choices.text: Thank the keeper in a long letter

effects.log: The reply is four words long. It is enough.

choices.text: Send three more spirit stones

effects.log: The tin on the high shelf is heavier by a few ounces of luck.

events.text: In the lecture-grove of a school you have only just joined, a story is told about an old cultivator who hid a child of the enemy in a crane-loft during the Isle War. You have never heard it. Your hands, folded in your lap, know every word, and the feather in the story, and the grey of it.

choices.text: Ask the lecturer where the tale comes from

effects.log: 'Everywhere,' says the lecturer. 'It was a long time ago.' You feel certain it was yesterday.

choices.text: Listen without a word

effects.log: The old warmth rises. You do not understand it, but you are glad of it.

events.text: A child at the foot of the stairs, a stranger, holds out a grey feather to you without a word. You take it. You hold it for a long time. You do not remember a house, a loft, a war. But you are crying, and you do not know why, and it is the kindest crying you can remember.

choices.text: Keep the feather

effects.log: It rests in your sleeve. It is warm.

choices.text: Give the feather back, gently

effects.log: The child nods as if this was the right answer. You feel a strange loss.

events.text: A lantern-seller at the market tells you that you have the look of one who once raised another's child. You laugh. You are young. But that night a dream shows you a loft of empty perches and a very small voice reciting numbers, and you wake with your hand outstretched, as if to reach down into a bell-tower.

choices.text: Write the dream down

effects.log: Pages of it. A whole house of ghosts, and one small child.

choices.text: Go back to sleep and leave it

effects.log: The dream does not return. The warmth stays.

events.text: At the morning offering a mortal child offers you a rice-cake and says your name, and you cannot return the courtesy. Those you love stand around the altar, and where their names lived there is only a smooth place, like a stone in a stream. In the Book of Fates, open on its stand, your own page has been scraped clean along one margin. A thin smell of ink hangs in the air.

choices.text: Run a finger down the scraped margin

effects.log: The parchment is warm. Someone has been very careful.

choices.text: Fold the page shut and say nothing

effects.log: The altar-bell rings. You answer the child's smile with your own.

events.text: You turned a leaf of the Unwritten Canon, the one page that no god is permitted to read, because the Canon says what has not yet been written, and you wished to know. Now you know. And the price is plain: every name that was ever written on your heart is a blank line. The page has closed itself. Your hands are ink to the wrists.

choices.text: Wash your hands in the temple font

effects.log: The ink will not wash. It sinks in, and becomes a faint grey tracery.

choices.text: Count the faces that you still know

effects.log: There are many. You write 'someone' under each, in careful letters.

events.text: Your divinity outgrew its vessel in the night. A new domain opened in you like a flower, too big for the garden, and the overflow poured out through every old attachment. In the morning your power is clear and your hands are steady. It is only that the names of those you love have gone out with the tide, leaving shells.

choices.text: Sit in the sanctuary and breathe

effects.log: The overflow settles. The shells stay shells.

choices.text: Go to your people, nameless as they are

effects.log: They hold you without a word. It is a better welcome than names.

events.text: Your Divine Consort has begun marking the household with small signs: a crescent over the door, a circle on the bed-post, a crooked star on your cup. Each is the sign you would have used to call to each other across a crowd. You trace them in the dark with a fingertip. 'I know you,' the Consort says softly, from the doorway. 'That will do for now.'

choices.text: Hold the signs against your chest

effects.log: They are rough. They are warm.

choices.text: Make a sign of your own in return

effects.log: A new one, a spiral. It is used for ages.

events.text: God-Touched children grow quickly, and yours have noticed that you call each of them 'darling' and never anything else. Today the youngest spells out a name on a sheet of rice-paper, in a bold childish hand, and pushes it across the table. 'This one is mine,' the child says. 'You can use it. I do not mind.'

choices.text: Read the name aloud and watch it slip

effects.log: It slides off your tongue as water off oiled silk. The child nods, gravely.

choices.text: Pin the paper to the wall

effects.log: It hangs where you can see it every morning.

events.text: A mortal priest in the valley you have favoured for centuries asks for guidance in a prayer that begins with your name and then with someone else's, a name the priest assumes you know. You do not. The prayer hangs in the air, unanswered. For the first time in your age, you hesitate before answering a prayer.

choices.text: Answer the part you can

effects.log: The priest is satisfied. You are not.

choices.text: Ask the priest to say the name again

effects.log: The priest does. It falls away from you like a coin through water.

events.text: At the Court of Vows a clerk reads out the register of those who stand before the Court today, and you reach for the name of the one who is to speak on your side. A brief silence. The clerk looks up. 'Shall we say, the defender?' the clerk offers kindly. The Court goes on. You are grateful, and you are not.

choices.text: Thank the clerk quietly

effects.log: A small courtesy returned.

choices.text: Resolve to find the cause this year

effects.log: The resolve is firmer than usual.

events.text: In the Hall of Records a very old archivist whispers that a scribe of the Heavenly Court went rogue long ago, a faceless clerk who struck names from the Book in exchange for the stolen faith of those they belonged to. The archivist will not say the scribe's name. 'Look for the page with the clean margin,' the archivist says. 'The scribe always leaves a margin.'

choices.text: Ask where the clean margins are found

effects.log: 'Everywhere,' says the archivist. 'That is the trouble.'

choices.text: Offer the archivist a cup of ambrosia

effects.log: The archivist takes it, and tells you a little more.

events.text: In the lowest scriptorium of the Book of Fates, you find a desk with no chair and a quill with no hand. The quill moves of its own accord, a hair's breadth above the parchment, tracing the shapes of names it does not write. A faceless figure stands in the doorway, watching it work. The figure bows once, politely, and does not leave.

choices.text: Bow back, and ask a question

effects.log: The figure tilts its blank face to listen.

choices.text: Take the quill's hovering line and follow it

effects.log: It leads to a locked drawer.

events.text: The Faceless Scribe sits at last across a low table from you and sets down a ledger. In it, in small tidy letters, is every name it has taken, and beside each, a price. 'A name is a thing of weight,' says the Scribe in a voice like the rustle of pages. 'I will return yours if you can tell me what they weigh. Not in faith. In truth.'

choices.text: Tell the Scribe what each one means to you

effects.log: It takes the whole night. The Scribe writes none of it down.

choices.text: Offer the Scribe a story it has not heard

effects.log: The Scribe's blank face lifts slightly.

events.text: A doorkeeper of the Heavenly Court tells you, frankly, that the Unwritten Canon has eaten gods before. 'It does not erase,' she says. 'It borrows. Whatever it takes it files in its own margin, in a hand no one else can read. If you find the file, you find the names.' She suggests the Canon's reading-room, at the bottom of the lowest stair.

choices.text: Ask how to read an unreadable hand

effects.log: She smiles. 'With a lamp that does not mind the dark.'

choices.text: Ask what happens if the Canon does not give them back

effects.log: She does not answer at once.

events.text: The Canon's reading-room is a cube of black glass, lit by a single lamp that gives no light. Inside, pages float at eye level, marked with faint grey scrawls. You find your own name on one, and under it a list of smudges. Each smudge has a faint warmth. They are the names, filed in a hand that is not a hand.

choices.text: Touch the nearest smudge

effects.log: It tingles. For a moment you almost have it.

choices.text: Copy the smudges onto a clean page

effects.log: The copy is as blurred as the original.

events.text: Holding your lamp that does not mind the dark, you read the Canon's marginal hand, one smudge at a time, and each yields a syllable. The syllables do not make a name. They make a sound, like a stone dropped in a well. Then you understand: the names are not in the writing. They are in the silence between the strokes.

choices.text: Read the silences

effects.log: It takes a long night. You hear the shape of the first name, almost.

choices.text: Ask the Canon for them, in the old tongue

effects.log: The Canon is silent, then sighs.

events.text: A physician-god of the Laughing River takes your pulse of divinity and shakes her head, smiling kindly. 'You overflowed,' she says. 'Your names did not vanish. They were spilled. Everything that overflows pools somewhere, in the lowest place nearby.' She recommends a pilgrimage along the course of your own power, downhill.

choices.text: Ask how to follow it

effects.log: 'Walk down your own river,' she says.

choices.text: Ask what to do if the pool is far

effects.log: 'Then you walk,' she says.

events.text: Downhill from your sanctuary, in a quiet vale you have never visited, the earth is dark and damp where your power spilled. Small flowers have grown there. Each is a different colour. At the heart of the vale is a still pool, and in it, drifting, are small bright motes. Each is a name. They will not come to your hand.

choices.text: Wade into the pool

effects.log: The motes part around you.

choices.text: Sit on the bank and wait

effects.log: The motes drift closer in the hush.

events.text: The physician-god of the Laughing River teaches you the rite of the Gathering Cup: you must hold each mote in your hand for the length of a breath and speak, to it, what it means. Then it will go home. The first three motes slip out of your palm like fish. The fourth rests a moment. You feel something shift, deep and faint.

choices.text: Finish the cup

effects.log: It takes the whole night.

choices.text: Rest and gather the rest tomorrow

effects.log: Rest helps. The vale sings in the dark.

events.text: The Faceless Scribe closes the ledger and, one by one, dips its quill and writes the names back in your page's margin, in a hand you suddenly recognise. Each one lands in you like a bell. The Scribe gives a small bow and fades like ink into water. The page of the Book is whole. On the margin, in small letters: with thanks for the truth.

choices.text: Say each name aloud to the empty room

effects.log: The room hums back.

choices.text: Leave a cup of ambrosia at the empty desk

effects.log: In the morning it is gone.

events.text: The last syllable falls into place in the silence of the black-glass room. The pages in the Canon turn blank, one by one, with a sound like snow settling, and the names go back into you through your open hands. You walk up the lowest stair into the light of day, saying them. The ink on your hands has gone.

choices.text: Go and find them at once

effects.log: You run.

choices.text: Sit a while and let it settle

effects.log: The names are yours. They stay.

events.text: The last mote closes in your palm and the vale goes still. Then, quietly, the flowers begin to close their petals, one colour at a time, and a warm tide rises in you from below, filling the old rooms of the memory with names. Each in its place, each in its own light. You walk up out of the vale, saying them softly.

choices.text: Walk to the sanctuary and call them

effects.log: They come at once.

choices.text: Plant a seed in the vale

effects.log: In thanks.

events.text: A whole festival season is spent chasing a witness who turns out to have been a copy-clerk, hired by the Court only to blot pages. The clerk weeps when you confront the point, and begs you not to tell the overseers. You let the clerk go. There is no clue here. There is only a tired mortal-minded soul who needed the wage.

choices.text: Pay the clerk's debt and send them home

effects.log: A small mercy, a poor trade for a lost year.

choices.text: Report nothing and walk on

effects.log: The year is spent.

events.text: The oracle of the Nine Wells, consulted at great cost in faith, answers your question with another: 'Which name did you expect to hear first?' You do not know. You realise you have never asked yourself, and the oracle will say no more. The faith is spent. You walk back through the wells in the rain.

choices.text: Think about the question on the way

effects.log: By the last well you have half an answer.

choices.text: Curse the oracle gently

effects.log: It does not answer to that either.

events.text: A theory about the curse takes hold of you for months: a pattern of numbers in the Book, a recurring figure in the margin. You chart it, map it, bring it to a senior archivist who looks at it for a long time. 'It is a stain,' she says, 'from a leaking inkpot. It appears on every page in this wing.' You laugh until you cry.

choices.text: Laugh with her

effects.log: It does you good.

choices.text: Burn the chart

effects.log: The smoke smells faintly of ink.

events.text: You gather the motes of your lost names in the Gathering Cup and, at the moment of closing your hand, a gust of divine wind from some other god's festival scatters them across the vale. They sink into the grass like seeds. You kneel for an hour, picking at them, until your fingers bleed light. None can be recovered. Not tonight.

choices.text: Plant the vale with flowers to mark the spot

effects.log: In spring the whole vale will bloom.

choices.text: Go home and plan a calmer day

effects.log: A day without wind.

events.text: The Faceless Scribe's price turns out to be a name of your own, one you will not give. You refuse, and the scribe closes the ledger without protest, with a nod almost of respect. 'Another day,' the scribe says, and is gone from the room as ink leaves a page. The ledger remains on the table, unlocked, unreadable.

choices.text: Leave the ledger where it is

effects.log: It is a trap, or a test, or a gift.

choices.text: Take it and run

effects.log: The ledger bites your wrist with cold.

events.text: The Canon's reading-room has changed its lock, and the lamp that does not mind the dark has gone out. The doorkeeper shrugs, apologetic. 'The Canon sealed itself in the night. It does that. I'm sorry.' You stand at the black glass door for a long time and see only your own face, worn, patient, turned slightly away.

choices.text: Wait by the door through the night

effects.log: The door does not open.

choices.text: Leave a prayer on the threshold

effects.log: It goes unanswered, but it is a prayer.

events.text: A moth settles on the rim of your wine-cup at the Court's evening feast, and you watch it pat its wings, and for no reason a name drops into you whole, like a pearl into a bowl. You say it into the cup. '{nc_name}.' Someone across the table lets out a long breath and puts down a cup. 'There,' the one across says. 'There you are.'

choices.text: Say it again, across the table

effects.log: {nc_name}, and the room stills to hear it.

choices.text: Raise your cup to {nc_name}

effects.log: The toast is brief and unsteady and perfect.

events.text: It comes during a funeral of a mortal you once favoured, in the valley where the ashes are given to the wind. A widow reads out the dead man's friends, one by one, and as the list passes, a name inside it unlocks in you. {nc_name}. You say it aloud, at the graveside. The widow glances over. So do many others. One of them is crying.

choices.text: Go to {nc_name} when the rite is done

effects.log: You say it again, quietly, nose to nose.

choices.text: Finish the rite first, in silence

effects.log: Some names can wait until after the wind.

events.text: A prayer rises to you, from an unknown mouth, the plain kind that asks nothing: only that a certain person be well. It names the person. {nc_name}. You catch the name on its way up like a falling coin and, before it can fall through, you say it three times aloud. Heaven's rafters take the sound and hold it.

choices.text: Answer the prayer: they are well

effects.log: The answer is true, and takes the whole day to deliver.

choices.text: Seek out the one who prayed

effects.log: A mortal child in a far valley, who grins.

events.text: The dead are not in the Book, but they are in the margin, and there they keep their names whole. You find one of your own, once, in a clerk's notes, and cannot read it.
